caption_lines: This is Bakasana B (crane asana, also called crow). You jump from hands and feet straight onto your arms, knees on your upper arms.
Strong arms help, but they are not enough. The breath and a strong middle hold you there.
Follow the words on screen. Breathe in and jump. Hold the belly. Breathe out slowly as the knees touch the arms. Then stay for five breaths.
Bandha means a light lock low in the belly. You breathe with it and push back with it. Then you breathe out and land.
This was our Saturday led Intermediate class (the second Ashtanga series) at AYBKK with @boonchutanti. Led means the teacher calls every breath and the whole room moves together.

caption_lines: A teacher who always lifts you into the asana, without showing you how, is not really helping.
A good teacher helps at the start, so you feel what the asana should feel like. Then it is on you.
Don't just wait for the teacher. Ask: what do I need to fix to do this myself?
Then try, fall, and try again. You learn to fall before you can balance. That is how the asana becomes yours.
Teachers too: let your students fall, figure it out and get back up. Teach them to be capable, not dependent.
